children: Fears about the AI buildout are "way overblown," says Dan Ives, partner and analyst at Yorkville Ives, in a note. "We are in a market environment in which any negative data point or hint of nervousness causes panic for the tech sector as this multi-trillion AI foundation buildout is tied to a handful of major tech players," says Ives. Higher rates don't change underlying demand for the buildout, even though it does matter for debt and how the investment gets financed, Ives adds. U.S. stock futures show signs of recovering sentiment in Asian trade. Futures tied to the Nasdaq, Dow Jones Industrial Average and S&P 500 climb 1.4%, 0.4% and 0.7%, respectively. (kimberley.kao@wsj.com)
